title: Deep assessments
description: Repos and models evaluated in depth, with warnings and what to steal.

items.name: atlas-gic
items.description: Self-improving trading agent framework: 4 agent layers, evolutionary prompt selection scored by Sharpe ratio, regime-specific cohorts, automatic specialist spawning. Claude Sonnet + FMP/Finnhub/Polygon/FRED.
items.verdictNote: steal the architecture, do not deploy
why: Prompt variants competing on a measured score (same idea as dspy + golden set)
Automatic retirement of bottom performers, which our Improver only suggests today
Spawn a specialist when the same gap repeats - a clean trigger rule for the swarm
Regime-specific cohorts: a prompt tuned in one regime is not tuned for another

warnings: The +22% over 173 days backtest is self-reported, unaudited, single-window; stars do not validate returns
Autonomous self-improving loop next to real money is the highest risk category in this brief
Apply the selection loop to extraction accuracy, listings and content - not to a live account

items.name: threejs-particle-fluids
items.description: MIT-licensed GPU particle fluid/cloth/smoke simulation in Three.js using WebGPU and TSL; nine presets, live controls, perf diagnostics; CC0 bundled assets
why: Effects technique and preset structure for future visual work

warnings: WebGPU mandatory with NO WebGL fallback - disqualifying for indie browser games that must run on phones and older laptops
4 stars, 0 forks: unproven
Revisit when WebGPU support is broad enough that no fallback is needed

items.name: Jev ecosystem (agents/memory/safety/tools/open models)
items.description: Official TypeSafe org publishes JS and Python SDKs, an agent-skills repo and system-one-adapter-python, each at roughly 15-35 stars. Community projects listed by the user arrived truncated and could not be opened.
why: typesafe-ai/system-one-adapter-python: drop-in TypeSafe client backed by ordinary LLM APIs - design and test the Jev gate against the golden set using Haiku BEFORE buying a key or adding a sixth vendor

warnings: Jev launched 2026-09-15; every project here is at most two weeks old
Memory/compaction projects overlap decisions already made (Supabase canonical, one memory layer)
Guard project overlaps our accuracy guard
Open-model clones matter only if Jev pricing or access changes
jev-trader carries the same live-money warning as atlas-gic
Community links unverified - treat awesome-lists as a map of attempts, not recommendations

items.name: UniMate (articulated motion generation)
items.url: https://linzhanmou.com/unimate/ ; arXiv 2609.05415 ; code MIT, weights+dataset on HuggingFace
items.description: SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 paper (Princeton/UC Berkeley/MIT). Rigged 3D asset + text prompt -> motion for ARBITRARY skeletons, no per-skeleton fine-tuning. Topology-aware diffusion transformer trained on UniML3D (13,006 sequences, creatures and objects). Zero-shot motion editing, in-betweening, expansion.
items.verdictNote: high potential for indie 3D games, blocked on training-data licensing
why: Targets indie-game's most expensive step: animation, which is the hard part of a weekly release cadence
Arbitrary skeletons is the key differentiator - most motion models are human-mocap only and cannot animate a dragon, cat or mech
Zero-shot in-betweening and editing would cut per-asset animation work substantially if clearable

warnings: MIT code does NOT make the weights commercially clear: training data is Mixamo (Adobe terms) + Objaverse-XL (per-object licences) + Truebones ZOO (commercial licence); repo instructs users to comply with source licences
Selling a game containing this model's output is an unsettled question - needs a lawyer before any paid release; answer may differ for free portal vs paid Steam
BLOCKING UNKNOWN: is the target game 2D or 3D? If 2D sprite games, skeletal motion synthesis is irrelevant
VRAM requirements unstated; diffusion transformer on an 8GB 4060 shared with ComfyUI and VoiceStudio is not a safe assumption
Export format unverified - value depends on glTF/FBX/BVH importing cleanly into a custom web engine or Godot
Posted ~2026-09-14, roughly two weeks old; research code, not a production dependency for weekly shipping
extra.unblockedAlternative: Mixamo's own library is free and explicitly licensed for commercial game use (humanoid). For non-humanoid, hand-authored Blender cycles or procedural animation; a small reusable cycle library beats an unclearable research model for a weekly cadence.

items.name: AERIS-10 (PLFM_RADAR)
items.description: Open-source 10.5 GHz PLFM phased array radar; 3 km and 20 km variants; +/-45 deg electronic beam steering, 360 deg mechanical scan; Xilinx XC7A50T FPGA + STM32F746; Python GUI with maps; GPS/IMU. Alpha / work in progress.
why: Requires custom multi-layer RF PCBs at 10.5 GHz vs current off-the-shelf ESP32/nRF52840 modules
Requires VHDL/Verilog FPGA work; user prefers no-code and has negligible coding experience
Requires VNA and spectrum analyser past 10 GHz; thousands in parts plus test gear
25.4k stars against 348 commits and Alpha badge: viral ahead of maturity, designs unproven

legalBlockers: Transmitting at 10.5 GHz with PAs at km range is not licence-exempt in Canada; verify with ISED licence-exempt standards; amateur licence is the only realistic hobby route
Radar is dual-use; a 20 km phased array may fall under Canada's Export Control List, restricting kit sales, board shipping and cross-border design-file sharing
patternsToSteal: CERN-OHL-P (hardware) + MIT (software) licence split - copy for the LoRa find-my-car release
Two-tier product ladder (short-range / long-range from one architecture) as the kit pricing model
Python GUI with map integration - reusable for the find-my-car tracker UI
GPS + IMU fusion pattern - same problem the tracker solves
Open-hardware repo structure: docs layout, contribution guidelines, status badges

shippableAlternative.name: Seeed MR60BHA2 60 GHz mmWave sensor
shippableAlternative.why: Certified module paired with XIAO ESP32C6, maintained ESPHome component, no RF design needed; upgrades the DFRobot baby camera into a contactless breathing-and-presence monitor inside existing ESP32 skills and budget
shippableAlternative.caution: Keep wording descriptive; a movement and breathing-rate sensor is not a medical device and must not be sold as one

items.name: Jev (TypeSafe AI), launched 2026-09-15
items.description: System One model: typed, calibrated decisions; generates no text
items.why: 'Cannot hallucinate' means schema-constrained only; it can still pick the wrong option Vendor benchmark 67.8% vs Opus 5 73.1%, self-run and unreproduced Adds a sixth vendor; wire it behind LiteLLM as a gate on one workflow and compare against the golden set

extra.category: System One model: typed, calibrated decisions; generates no text

api.price: $0.042 per M input tokens; output free

replacesInOurStack: classification, routing, scoring, tagging currently sent to Qwen or Haiku
first-pass compliance gate before Sonnet review
doesNotReplace: field and number extraction (returns no strings)
accuracy guard arithmetic and hard limits (stay in code)

economics.batching: TypeSafe cookbook: 13 questions in one call = 12.2x cheaper, 10x faster than sequential
economics.realSaving: Tier 1 is already free local Qwen; the win is gating Sonnet review — roughly 80% less review spend, about $10-40/mo at full volume
economics.status: estimate; measure in model_calls before trusting

caveats: 'Cannot hallucinate' means schema-constrained only; it can still pick the wrong option
Vendor benchmark 67.8% vs Opus 5 73.1%, self-run and unreproduced
Adds a sixth vendor; wire it behind LiteLLM as a gate on one workflow and compare against the golden set
extra.promptScreenshotNote: The circulating prompt is partly advertising for agenkit.xyz, a paid subscription product; Jev works without it. Its autonomous live-trading premise is a separate risk category — paper-trade first and keep it out of a finance-education brand.

items.name: RSIGame
items.description: Paper arXiv 2609.39045 (Sept 30 2026) + Apache-2.0 repo (28k lines Python). Loop per round: Explore (agent plays the built game, records logs/frames) -> Diagnose (one objective with most headroom) -> Edit (repair agent) -> Verify (independent agent replays; did it land, did anything regress). Outer 'Global Quality Monitor' keeps the best checkpoint and stops after K=3 checkpoints with no new champion. Evolving checklist of what the task asked for. Targets Godot 4 and Phaser. Second half: distils successful sessions into a LoRA on Qwen3.8-27B.
items.verdictNote: reference, not adopt-to-run. Steal five patterns now; revisit the code if weights/corpus are released and indie web-game games run on Godot.
items.why: Champion + saturation stop: keep the best build seen; stop after 3 checkpoints with no improvement. Apply to every swarm self-improve loop (Printables, finance-education shorts, indie web-game polish) - caps token spend and prevents late rounds undoing earlier gains Independent verifier: the agent that checks a change is not the one that made it, and must test for regressions, not just 'did it work' 'Silence does not write' checklist: an item not observed this round keeps its status; only evidence moves it. Fixes oscillating scores from noisy LLM judges (they measured 10% of items flipping between readings of the same trace) One objective per round: diagnose the single place with most headroom, edit against that only Cost metering through one loopback proxy that logs every call (prompt/completion/cached/reasoning tokens, dollars). A LiteLLM router with a cost-logging table already does the same; confirm cached and reasoning tokens are captured Hygiene to copy into Claude Code handoff: 'rsigame check' preflight before a run; test that scans the repo for secrets/personal paths; test that resolves every import including those inside functions; 3-layer config (defaults -> experiment -> env)

warnings: Numbers are the authors' own, on their own benchmark (GameCraft-Bench, 140 tasks), scored by an LLM judge; no independent reproduction yet. Repo has 6 stars and is 2 days old

Headline 'Qwen3.8-27B beats GPT-5.5 one-shot, 11x fewer generation tokens' needs 4x H100 80GB training and is about generation tokens after fine-tuning, not total loop cost. Not reproducible on an an 8 GB GPU
Weights, supervised corpus and base games are 'coming soon' pending the authors' company review; only table artefacts are published

`rsigame develop <game>` only accepts names from the benchmark's tasks/ folder (141 tasks). Running it on an existing game means writing them up as benchmark tasks (spec, base project, scripted demo inputs) - unverified how much work

Needs Godot 4 (or Node + OpenGame for Phaser) and an OpenRouter key; indie web-game in-house a custom web game engine is not supported without writing an adapter (the authors say the engine-specific part is ~900 of 48k lines)
No cost-per-game figure published. Their runs were 30-64 rounds with up to 1800 s repair budgets; run one game with a hard spend cap before committing

Code quality: strong design documentation and tests of the key logic, but declared Python >=3.11 while project_map.py uses 3.12-only f-string syntax (fails to compile on 3.11 and breaks 2 tests); ~6 undefined-name bugs in rarely-run scripts; huge functions (one_round 398 lines, explore 408); only ~1k lines of tests for 28k of source
Dependency licences checked: GameCraft-Bench Apache-2.0, OpenGame Apache-2.0 (per authors' NOTICE, not independently opened)

items.name: REA
items.description: MIT MCP server and CLI that connects agents to Ghidra, IDA, Hopper, JEB, JADX, Apktool, Binwalk/Unblob, GDB, TShark, mitmdump, adb and a browser: one entry point for binaries, Electron,.NET, Android and websites. 2,633 commits, 40.8k forks. Install: npx rea-agents setup (changes your agent config, keeps backups).
items.verdictNote: CONDITIONAL ADOPT: the one entry point if you do RE at all, installed only inside an isolated VM.
items.why: One MCP instead of five separate bridges Commercial tools (IDA, Hopper, JEB) are optional and must be bought separately

warnings: Star count on the page is 170.7k but a banner says 110k: popularity figures are inconsistent; neither is an audit
Runtime capture runs the target with your user permissions: never on a production server or a machine with API keys
Decompiled code you send to the agent goes to the model provider

items.name: Ghidra
items.description: Free decompiler and disassembler (Apache-2.0); needs JDK 25. No built-in AI; agents reach it through GhidraMCP or REA.
items.verdictNote: ADOPT inside the RE VM (free core tool).
items.why: Audit your own builds and firmware

warnings: Large Java install; keep in the VM

items.name: GhidraMCP
items.description: Apache-2.0 bridge: Ghidra plugin + HTTP server (localhost:8080) + Python MCP; headless mode via PyGhidra. 64 commits. Needs Ghidra 12.1.4.
items.verdictNote: ADOPT as the lightweight alternative to REA when you only need binaries.
items.why: Simpler than REA; fewer moving parts

warnings: HTTP server has no stated authentication: keep it on localhost

items.name: mitmproxy
items.description: MIT interactive HTTPS-intercepting proxy (mitmproxy, mitmdump, mitmweb).
items.verdictNote: ADOPT now: the most useful tool in this list for you.
items.why: Debug your own Public API MCP and n8n calls See exactly what the IoT devices, games and apps send (privacy claims, hidden telemetry in tools you install) Consulting: authorised traffic reviews

warnings: Install its certificate only on test devices; remove after
Do not use it to lift other services' private APIs into the catalogue

items.name: ImHex
items.description: Hex editor with a pattern language for binary formats (GPL-2.0, parts LGPL).
items.verdictNote: REFERENCE: useful hex editor; the post's 'with MCP server' is NOT in its README (a third-party jmpnop/imhexMCP exists, unchecked).
items.why: Inspect save files and asset formats of your own games

warnings: GPL: fine to use, careful if you ever ship code derived from it

items.name: ILSpy
items.verdictNote: CONDITIONAL: only for.NET/Unity builds you own or are authorised to inspect.
items.why: Check what your own Unity/.NET builds expose if indie web-game ever ships one

warnings: Decompiling other people's games to copy code is infringement

items.name: Frida
items.description: Runtime hooking toolkit for desktop and mobile with Python/Node bindings.
items.verdictNote: SKIP for now: powerful but high-risk; revisit for testing your own mobile apps.
items.why: Runtime tests of your own apps

warnings: Licence not named on the repo page; injection into apps you do not own breaks their terms

items.name: Android Reverse Engineering skill
items.description: Apache-2.0 Claude Code skill: decompiles APK/XAPK/JAR/AAR with jadx (optional Vineflower/Fernflower) and lists HTTP endpoints, auth headers, tokens and signing schemes. 31 commits. Disclaims misuse.
items.verdictNote: CONDITIONAL: own apps or written client authorisation only.
items.why: Security review of an app you build or a client asks you to test

warnings: Using it to find another company's private API and then calling it breaks their terms and can break Canadian law; never feed results into the public API catalogue

items.name: Universal Modder
items.description: MIT skills, CLI and a fal MCP to mod PC games you own: engine playbooks (Unity, Unreal,.NET/XNA, Godot, Source, Bethesda, Minecraft...), fal-generated art/3D/audio, in-game testing, showcase videos. Refuses anti-cheat, DRM and online cheating. 193 commits.
items.verdictNote: REFERENCE: read its engine playbooks to learn how games are structured; modding others' games is not a business line for you.
items.why: Engine knowledge for indie web-game 3D move Possible content idea: 'AI mods a classic' videos, only for games whose EULA allows mods

warnings: fal asset generation costs money (price not stated)
Respect each game's EULA; single-player only

items.name: Cpp2IL
items.description: MIT, work-in-progress tool that reverses Unity IL2CPP builds back to.NET DLLs for ILSpy.
items.verdictNote: SKIP: WIP and only relevant to Unity games you do not make.

warnings: Major rewrite in progress
